title: PC-02 validation session record
description: One validation session with one domain expert, moderated by one moderator, over documents drawn from fixtures/validation/PC-02. The protocol this schema records is docs/program/validation/PC-02_PROTOCOL.md. Every session record validates against this schema; a record that does not is not pooled, because a field a moderator invented is a field the other moderator did not fill.

findings.description: Every finding the system published, in the order it was reviewed. May be empty only if the system published none across the whole session, which is itself a result.

envelope_refusals.description: One record per negative-envelope document offered. Excluded from every finding denominator and from every gate that counts measurable documents.

deviations.description: Every departure from the protocol, including questions asked outside the closed set. Required, and may be empty - but empty means the moderator asserts there were none, not that nobody looked.

label.description: The three finding labels fixed by PROTOTYPE_PROFILE.md section 9. There is no fourth, and no 'partially useful'. A finding that tempts one is 'unclear'.

rationale.description: The expert's own words for why, recorded as spoken rather than paraphrased. At least 15 characters: a rationale of 'ok' does not let a second reader check the label.

moderator_id.description: Pseudonymous. Needed to compute inter-moderator agreement, which is the whole reason this protocol is written the way it is.

expert_id.description: Pseudonymous. No name, employer or contact detail enters the record.

reviews_ar_documents.description: Whether the expert reviews AR volumes as part of their actual work. An expert who does not is still worth hearing, and their records are reported separately rather than pooled.

build_commit.description: The commit the application was run from. Without it the session cannot be re-read against the code that produced it.

document_order.description: The labels of the measurable documents in the order presented, taken from the pre-registered rotation table in the protocol. Recorded rather than chosen, so order effects are comparable between sessions instead of being confounded with the moderator.

calibration_completed.description: Whether the calibration pass on the PC-01 baseline fixture was completed before the first PC-02 document. False invalidates the session for pooling.

ground_truth_withheld.description: The moderator asserts that neither they nor the expert saw corpus_manifest.json, any seeded-issue list or any control list before or during the session. False invalidates the session for pooling: a moderator who knows the answer cannot un-know it while phrasing a question.

review_seconds.description: Wall-clock from opening the finding list to the last label recorded, excluding any interruption recorded below.

time_box_reached.description: Whether the per-document time box was hit. A document that hit it is reported with its labels and separately flagged, never silently averaged in.

expert_suspected_issues.description: Issues the expert believes the document contains that the system did NOT report, captured before any ground truth is revealed. This is the only false-negative evidence a session can produce from the expert's side; the manifest supplies the rest afterwards.

would_use_output.description: Answer to protocol question D4 exactly as scripted: whether the expert would have used this finding list on a real document of this kind.

evidence_location_correct.description: Whether the quotation the finding cites is actually where it says it is, judged by the expert opening it. 'not_checked' is honest and usable; a guess is not.

expert_would_have_raised_it.description: The professional-usefulness question, asked separately from the label. A finding can be correct and still not worth raising, and PC-01 could not tell those apart.

navigation_steps.description: Interactions needed to get from the finding to its evidence in the document. Feeds the navigation-friction metric in PROTOTYPE_PROFILE.md section 9.

refused.description: Whether the upload or run was refused at all. An accepted negative-envelope document is a defect, not a finding.

rule_named_in_message.description: Whether the refusal identified the rule rather than failing generically. 'Something went wrong' is a refusal that teaches the user nothing.

message_quoted.description: The refusal message verbatim, so two sessions can be compared on wording rather than on the moderator's summary of it.

ocr_silently_substituted.description: Whether the product silently OCR'd or partially read a document it should have refused. PROTOTYPE_PROFILE.md section 7.1 forbids this outright.

blocking_capability.description: Which missing stage or capability prevents real use (PROTOTYPE_PROFILE.md section 9). Chosen from a closed list so two sessions can be counted together, with free text beside it so a reason nobody anticipated is not lost.

next_investment.description: Whether audit depth or document comparison is the next highest-value investment, asked as a forced choice with a reason.

failures_observed.description: Failures seen during the session and what each would actually need. Feeds the retry / Attempt-fencing / remote-execution question.

expert_closing_comment.description: The answer to the single open closing question, recorded verbatim. It is the last thing asked and the only unscripted one, so it cannot contaminate any label.

affects.description: The document labels whose records this deviation touches, so the analyst can exclude exactly those rather than the whole session.
